summary: Unattributed hosted charges from postbacks during Private VPN outage — customer requests mapping and credit
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightGuide reports unexpected Hosted invoice line items for the billing period starting 2026-03-01. Charges are labeled as 'hosted: transient-unattributed' and total ~USD 3,120. Customer uses Redwood Private deployment (VPC) in us-west; they experienced a 23-minute VPN outage on 2026-03-05 (08:14–08:37 UTC) and observed failover to Hosted via smart routing.

Impact:
- Customer saw hosted charges that do not match any of their hosted API keys or org ids.
- These charges appear under an internal pooled account and were passed through to BrightGuide's consolidated invoice as 'unattributed-hosted'.
- Customer requests a full mapping of the postbacks during the outage window to confirm those tokens belong to their requests and to request a credit for the portion billed to the pooled account.

Environment:
- Private deployment: BrightGuide VPC ID bg-0912, Redwood Private v1.8.
- Hosted fallback configured: enabled, priority policy = prefer-private -> fallback-hosted.
- Billing: consolidated monthly invoice, invoicing account bg-invoice-01.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-05 08:14 UTC — BrightGuide reports VPN tunnel flapped (internal ticket BG-OPS-77).
2) Smart routing triggered fallback for ~23 minutes; some requests routed to Hosted endpoints.
3) Hosted metering recorded postbacks that lacked an org_id header due to an internal postback-translator bug (hypothesis).
4) Metering pipeline assigned these events to a transient internal pool (acct: hosted-transient-unnamed).
5) Invoice shows a line: "hosted: transient-unattributed — USD 3,120" dated 2026-03-06.

Logs / Observations (customer-provided):
- Example request id reported by customer: rq_20260305_08:19:43_bg_7a1b2c
- Customer timeline (attached): BG-OPS VPN event log excerpt.
- Customer's hosted API keys do not match invoice attribution.

Requested outcome:
- Map the hosted postback events during 08:14–08:37 UTC to BrightGuide's original requests (show request ids, timestamps, and token counts).
- If mapping confirms ownership, apply credit to remove the "transient-unattributed" line and re-attribute usage to BrightGuide so it appears under their private/hosted mix properly.
- Provide root cause and mitigation steps to avoid future unattributed postbacks during Private->Hosted failover.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:22 — Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket opened after BrightGuide escalated via support@. Collected invoice PDF and BG-OPS VPN event log. Assigned to billing investigator and routing SRE.

2026-03-10 16:05 — Liam O'Connor (Routing SRE): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: postback-translator service drops org_id when origin is private->hosted fallback if X-Org header is missing. Starting trace in routing logs for 2026-03-05 08:10–08:45 UTC.

2026-03-10 17:40 — Billing (Marta Ruiz): Noted invoice line under acct hosted-transient-unnamed. Will hold billing adjustment pending mapping. Marked for provisional credit if mapping confirms customer ownership.
2026-03-11 09:12 — BrightGuide (Evan Cho): Provided sample request ids and attached VPN event trace. Customer requests expedited resolution due to budget review meeting on 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12 11:03 — Liam O'Connor (Routing SRE): Found routed records in router-logs where org_id header was present at ingress but dropped by postback-translator service instance translator-17. Preserved request ids match customer's sample (rq_20260305_08:19:43_bg_7a1b2c).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 18:00 — Tracing: Use request id pattern rq_20260305_* to pull entries from router-logs and postback-queue. Found 412 postbacks in the window 08:14–08:37 UTC with missing org_id in postback payloads.

2026-03-11 19:10 — Correlation: Cross-referenced bg-0912 private deployment IP ranges with origin IPs of postbacks; 398/412 map to BrightGuide IP block. 14 appear to be other orgs. Conservative mapping approach: attribute only those with IP + request id match.

2026-03-11 20:25 — Root cause hypothesis: translator-17 uses a cached header schema that erroneously applied a transformation removing 'X-Org' when a certain proxy header (X-VPN-ROUTE) is present. Regression introduced in translator release v2.3.5 on 2026-03-05 07:54 UTC during canary push.

2026-03-12 08:40 — Reproduction: Locally replayed representative postback payloads through translator-17 binary with and without X-VPN-ROUTE header; confirmed org_id removal only when X-VPN-ROUTE present.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 13:15 — Immediate mitigation: Rolled back translator service to v2.3.4 in us-west and eu-west to stop further org_id drops. Monitoring set for next 48 hours. (deployments/rollback PR: github.com/redwood/translator/pull/423)

2026-03-12 14:00 — Attribution and credit plan: Billing confirmed 398 postbacks attributable to BrightGuide. Calculated affected token count = 1,042,560 tokens (~USD 2,970). Issued provisional invoice credit for USD 2,970 and removed 'transient-unattributed' line pending final audit. Remaining USD 150 corresponds to 14 ambiguous postbacks owned by other orgs — not credited.

2026-03-12 15:20 — Customer communication: Notified BrightGuide support contact (Evan Cho) of mapping results, provisional credit, and rollback. Provided instructions to request re-attribution if they have additional request ids. Scheduled post-incident follow-up meeting with SRE and billing on 2026-03-16.

Follow-ups (action items):
- Engineering to add defensive check in translator to preserve X-Org when X-VPN-ROUTE present (issue INT-5429).
- Billing to finalize credit and confirm ledger adjustment in accounting (ticket BILL-3981).
- Support to confirm BrightGuide receives corrected invoice PDF and reconcile in their accounts payable by 2026-03-18.
